## 2

I understand why some images can seem difficult to verify firsthand, especially when most of us rely on photographs and scientific institutions. But the evidence for a roughly spherical Earth doesn’t depend on space photos alone: ships disappear hull-first over the horizon, different stars are visible at different latitudes, Earth’s shadow on the Moon during lunar eclipses is round, and people have measured Earth’s curvature and circumnavigated the planet for centuries. These observations come from many independent sources, so faking photographs would not explain the broader evidence.

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made of many colors. When sunlight enters Earth’s atmosphere, it bumps into tiny air molecules. Blue light gets scattered in all directions more easily than most other colors, so blue light reaches our eyes from across the sky.

Violet is scattered even more, but our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some violet light is absorbed higher in the atmosphere. That is why the sky usually looks blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering much of the blue away; the reds and oranges are then more likely to reach us.

雨下了一整夜，城市像浸在一片深蓝色的水里。路灯被雨幕揉碎，昏黄的光在积水中轻轻摇晃。窗外的屋檐不断滴水，像有人耐心地敲着一面小鼓。偶尔汽车驶过，溅起白亮的水花，很快又消失在寂静里。风吹动树叶，带来潮湿的泥土气息。房间里只亮着一盏灯，书页摊在桌上，雨声把漫长的夜晚包裹得格外温柔。
